stories.title: Punjab land reforms project reaches 90pc progress
summary: ISLAMABAD: The World Bank-fin­a­n­ced Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhan­cement (Pulse) project has achieved 90 per cent physical progress, recording 69.9 million land rights in its information system against a target of 50.7 million, with 31pc registered in women’s names.

Approved in 2022 with financing of $150m, the project aims to establish a unified land registry linked to digital cadastral maps, forming the basis of a comprehensive land administration system covering urban and rural areas of Punjab.

The report identifies several environmental and social challenges in urban and peri-urban areas, including air pollution, contaminated drinking water, untreated wastewater, inadequate solid waste collection and disposal, and the expansion of cities over prime agricultural land.

stories.title: 4 guards of Sardar Khetran held after body recovered from Barkhan property
summary: QUETTA: Police said on Sunday they have detained four guards of former Balochistan minister Sardar Abdul Rehman Khetran following the reported recovery of a body from his property in Barkhan district.
On Nov 18, Barkhan police registered a case against Khetran; his two sons, Islam Shah and Abdul Rauf; and three other accomplices on charges of murder, kidnapping and illegal confinement.
Khan Muhammad Marri, a former guard of Khetran, had said the bodies were of his wife Granaz and two sons, alleging they were kept in private jails.

stories.title: Afghan tradition keeps grapes fresh for winter treat
summary: KALAKAN: On the outskirts of Afghanistan’s frenetic capital Kabul, Muhammad Saber Shojaei is carrying out a centuries-old task of preserving fistfuls of grapes to be eaten when winter bites.

Carefully putting a bunch of grapes in one of the discs, Shojaei added a second disc on top and sealed the disc with mud before placing it in a dark storage room. “In this way, Kanginas can keep grapes fresh from now until the spring,” said the farmer.
But in the depths of winter, Afghans living near the vineyards can buy them along the roadside or in nearby markets, and farming families can crack them open and enjoy fresh grapes.

Both the ordinances provide for the establishment of an executive committee comprising a chairman, vice chairman and other such members as nominated by the prime minister, in case of designated district, and by the governor of the province, in case of the remaining districts.

stories.title: Internet provider expects submarine cable repairs to be completed by Dec 6
summary: Internet service provider Transworld Associates has said repair work on an affected international submarine cable is expected to be completed by December 6, with users likely to experience slower internet speeds during peak hours until the work is finished.

The development follows an earlier announcement by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) that a fault had been reported in the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5) international submarine cable system, approximately 11 kilometres from Pakistan’s coast.
Internet monitoring organisation NetBlocks had also reported a decline in connectivity in Pakistan, saying the incident was consistent with a fault in the SMW5 international subsea cable system.

stories.title: Security forces kill 15 terrorists in Balochistan's Mastung district: state media
summary: Security forces have killed 15 terrorists during two separate operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district, state media reported on Saturday.
According to security sources cited by Radio Pakistan, five terrorists were killed in the first operation, while 10 others were eliminated in the second one.
Security forces remain committed to eradicating terrorism from Balochistan, and operations will continue until the last terrorist is eliminated, security sources asserted.

stories.title: CCD's school bag inspections in Punjab spark criticism on social media
summary: After the CCD set up a checking point outside a college in Lahore on Friday, it issued a press release on Saturday announcing a special campaign across educational institutions in Punjab to protect children from drugs, cigarettes, vapes and other intoxicating substances.

According to the press release by a CCD spokesperson, special checking desks have been established outside educational institutions, where students’ bags were searched to ensure that no intoxicating substances were taken inside, knowingly or unknowingly.

Former Punjab minister Arslan Khalid also questioned the presence of police personnel outside educational institutions, saying schools should not rely on police to discipline children. “Parents and teachers are enough to teach discipline to the children.

stories.title: Govt expenses squeeze development
summary: The ever-expanding administrative machinery of Pakistan is putting additional pressure on public finances at a time when the country needs to generate millions of jobs, attract private investment and accelerate development spending.

The report suggests that expanding administrative establishments without clearly defining responsibilities and financing arrangements could further increase government expenditure without necessarily improving public service delivery.

For Pakistan, where fiscal constraints continue to limit development spending and millions of new workers are entering the labour market, the effectiveness of government institutions is becoming an increasingly important part of the economic reform agenda.

stories.title: EU proposes 40b Euros cut to long-term budget
summary: The chairman of European Union leaders proposed further cuts to the European Commission's draft EU 2028-2034 budget on Saturday and suggested new revenue streams for the EU, including a digital tax, to help finance EU policies.
Costa's proposal mainly cuts the European Competitiveness Fund - aimed at helping make European industry more competitive against China and the United States - defence and external spending.

Friedrich Merz, the chancellor of Germany, which is the biggest net contributor to the budget and has repeatedly called for the budget to be slashed by hundreds of billions of euros, said the proposal was a first step, but still too high.

stories.title: Minister calls for secure data sharing among institutions
summary: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal has called for strengthening data-sharing mechanisms among government institutions to promote evidence-based policymaking, improve coordination and ensure effective utilisation of official statistics.

Chairing a meeting at the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) headquarters, he stressed the need for a secure mechanism for sharing data between PBS, federal ministries and public sector organisations.

Secretary Planning Dr Muhammad Tahir Noor said effective utilisation of PBS data was essential for informed policymaking, and he stressed the need for efficient data sharing with line ministries, provincial governments and other stakeholders.

summary: The challenge, he says, is not simply to make financing cheaper or relax eligibility conditions, but to create productive businesses capable of winning repeat orders, improving export prices and sustaining their presence in international markets.

stories.title: India's Congress warns of more protests against Meta after clashes with police outside its offices
summary: The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party on Saturday warned of more protests against Meta’s removal of some accounts and posts of its members, a day after clashing with police outside the US firm’s India offices.
Congress has long accused Meta and other social media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi’s government.

On Saturday, the Congress wing posted a video of its workers putting up a banner in central Delhi taking a dig at Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, referring to him as “Mark BJPberg” to allege the company’s favouritism towards Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party.

summary: China on Thursday renewed its call at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) to place the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its suicide wing, the Majeed Brigade, on the UNSC’s 1267 sanctions list.
China has renewed its call at the UN to place the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its Majeed Brigade on the UNSC’s 1267 sanctions list.

Her husband and their domestic worker were arrested as Hina’s family accused them of murdering her, while her father-in-law was questioned as part of the investigation.

stories.title: COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime
summary: The COP31 climate summit will either produce a good deal or no ​deal at all, the European Union's top climate official said on Saturday as talks stretched deep into overtime.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries ‌are struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, delaying an agreement at the two-week conference that had been scheduled to end on Friday.

Asked about the chances of no deal emerging, he said: "We will ​find out." The last major breakdown in UN climate talks came in Copenhagen in 2009, when countries failed to adopt the Copenhagen ​Accord by consensus in a setback for multilateral climate diplomacy.

stories.title: SICVD treats 22,639 heart attack patients, performs 1,626 surgeries in 10 months
summary: The Sindh Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (SICVD) treated 22,639 heart attack patients through angiography and angioplasty and performed 1,626 open-heart surgeries between January and October 2026, according to a statement issued by the institute.

During the 10-month period, the institute’s network of 30 chest pain units across Sindh handled 463,975 emergency cases, while its triage and emergency departments received a total of 598,401 patients, the statement said.
The institute’s catheterisation laboratories also performed diagnostic angiography on 7,210 patients, who were subsequently referred for medical management or surgery.

stories.title: FBI's criminal information database hacked, CNN reports
summary: The FBI is investigating a suspected breach of a nationwide database ​used by federal, state and local ‌law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information, CNN reported on Friday, citing two people briefed ​on the investigation.

The apparent compromise of the ​National Crime Information Centre database would ⁠mark the second intrusion involving an FBI ​system in recent months and the latest in ​a string of cyber incidents that have alarmed US officials over the past week.

stories.title: States agree to UN talks aiming to regulate 'killer robots' by 2028
summary: UN talks on regulating weapons with little or no human oversight ended on Saturday with a pledge for further discussions to develop new rules within two years, an outcome weakened by Russia's opposition and disappointing human ​rights groups.

Proponents had called for legally binding rules within a short timeframe to regulate weapons ​systems that can identify and engage targets with varying degrees of autonomy, ⁠sometimes called "killer robots".
"Delaying the creation of a legally binding instrument puts civilians and humanity at risk,” said Nicole van Rooijen, executive director at Stop Killer Robots, on the sidelines of ⁠the talks.

stories.title: Parliamentary affairs minister invites PTI to join NA electoral reforms committee
summary: The government on Saturday invited the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to join the National Assembly (NA) Electoral Reforms Committee (ERC), offering representation in proportion to the party’s strength in the lower house while rejecting its demand for equal representation.
The NA on October 16 passed a motion moved by Dr Chaudhry under Rule 244B to form a parliamentary committee comprising members from both houses to recommend electoral reforms.
The motion stipulated that parliamentary parties would be represented in proportion to their strength in Parliament.
